threshold: Start with the lowest-cost available setting that reliably passes the task checks. Compare eligible settings on the same task benchmark and version. As a guide, an upgrade should add about 5 points per doubling of benchmark cost, or about 75 Elo on GDPval. On a close call, favor the cheaper, faster setting when both meet the task requirements. Escalate when failures or rework justify it.

terra_guidance.heading: When to use GPT-6.1 Terra
terra_guidance.intro: Every number below is already sourced in this guide's task rows and news. API task costs do not measure subscription usage. Terra is available in Work, Codex and the API only, not in ChatGPT Chat.
items: **Scripted relays and ordinary branching tool workflows**: start with Terra low ($0.07, AutomationBench 56.2%). Terra medium scores 58% at $0.17 and adds 1.6 points for 2.43x the cost, which does not clear the upgrade rule. Use a higher effort only after a failed task check.
**General-purpose default**: Terra medium (AutomationBench 58% at $0.17). Sol medium adds 5 points at $0.36 (2.1x the cost), or 4.6 points per cost doubling, below the 5-point threshold.
**General agentic judgment on a budget**: Terra high ($0.26, index 42.4) is the cheaper choice next to Sol xhigh ($0.76, index 52).
**Do not pick Terra for facts, names, messages, money or records**: use Sol low ($0.16, AA-Omniscience 38) and verify consequential claims.
**Do not pick Terra for coding**: use Sol xhigh ($0.76, 54%).
